sanskrit: daśavṛkṣa muñcemam aṃhaso grāhyāś ca | atho enaṃ vanaspate jīvānāṃ lokam un naya ||
english: O ten-tree, release this one from distress and from the seizure-demon! And do thou, O lord of the forest, lead him up into the world of the living.

sanskrit: yaś cakāra sa niṣ karat sa eva subhiṣaktamaḥ | sa eva tubhyaṃ bheṣajaṃ cakāra bhiṣajāti ca ||
english: He who made it shall undo it — he alone is the most skillful physician; he it is who has made the remedy for thee, and who practises healing.

sanskrit: cītiṃ te devā avidan brahmāṇa uta vīrudhaḥ | cītiṃ te 'dyottamām avidan bhūmyām adhi ||
english: The gods, the brahman-sages, and the plants have found thy cure; they have found today thy highest cure upon the earth.

sanskrit: āgād ud agād ayaṃ jīvānāṃ vrātam apy agāt | abhūd u putrāṇāṃ pitā nṛṇāṃ ca bhagavattamaḥ ||
english: He has come, he has risen up, he has rejoined the company of the living; he has become once more the father of his sons, the most blessed one among men.

sanskrit: adhītim adhy agād ayam adhi jīvapurā agāt | śataṃ ca yasya vīrudhaḥ sahasram uta bheṣajā ||
english: This one has passed beyond affliction; he has gone to the citadel of the living — he whose plants number a hundred and whose remedies number a thousand.

sanskrit: dīrghāyutvāya bṛhate raṇāya- -ariṣyanto dakṣamāṇāḥ sadaiva | maṇiṃ viṣkandhadūṣaṇaṃ jaṅgiḍaṃ bibhṛmo vayam ||
english: For long life, for great exhilaration — ever unharmed and thriving — we wear the amulet jaṅgiḍa, the destroyer of viṣkandha.

sanskrit: jaṅgiḍo jambhād viśarād viṣkandhād abhiśocanāt | maṇiḥ sahasravīryaḥ pari ṇaḥ pātu viśvataḥ ||
english: From the crusher, from the bursting-pain, from viṣkandha, from tormenting affliction — may the amulet jaṅgiḍa, thousand-powered, guard us on all sides.

sanskrit: ayaṃ viṣkandhaṃ sahate ayaṃ rakṣo 'pa bādhate | ayaṃ no viśvabheṣajo jaṅgiḍaḥ pātv aṃhasaḥ ||
english: This one overpowers viṣkandha; this one drives away the rakṣas; may this jaṅgiḍa, the all-healer, protect us from distress.

sanskrit: devair dattena maṇinā jaṅgiḍena mayobhuvā | viṣkandhaṃ sarvā rakṣāṃsi vyāyāme sahāmahe ||
english: With the amulet jaṅgiḍa given by the gods, bestower of bliss, we overpower viṣkandha and all the rakṣas-demons in combat.

sanskrit: śaṇaś ca tvā jaṅgiḍaś ca viṣkandhād adhi muñcatām | araṇyād anya ābhṛtaḥ kṛṣyā anyo rasebhyaḥ ||
english: May śaṇa and jaṅgiḍa both release thee from viṣkandha — one brought from the forest, the other from the cultivated field, from their essences.

sanskrit: eha yantu paśavo ye pareyur vāyur yeṣāṃ sahacāraṃ jujoṣa | tvaṣṭā yeṣāṃ rūpadheyāni veda- -asmin tān goṣṭhe savitā ni yacchāt ||
english: Let the cattle that have strayed hence come hither — cattle whose companionship Vāyu has favored, whose forms Tvaṣṭṛ knows well; may Savitṛ settle them in this cattle-pen.

sanskrit: imaṃ goṣṭhaṃ paśavaḥ saṃ sravantu bṛhaspatir ā nayatu prajānan | sinīvālī nayatv āgram eṣām ājagmuṣo anumatir ni yacchāt ||
english: Let the cattle stream together into this pen; may Bṛhaspati lead them hither in his wisdom; may Sinīvālī lead them at their head, and may Anumati settle those that have returned.

sanskrit: saṃ saṃ sravantu paśavaḥ sam aśvā uta pūruṣāḥ | saṃ dhānyasya yā sphātiḥ saṃsrāvyeṇa haviṣā juhomi ||
english: Let the cattle stream together, let the horses and men stream together; let the prosperity of the grain come together — with the oblation that causes confluence I offer.

sanskrit: saṃ siñcāmi gavāṃ kṣīraṃ sam ājyena balaṃ rasam | saṃsiktā asmākaṃ vīrā mayi gāvaś ca gopatau ||
english: I pour together the milk of the cattle; I pour together strength and essence with ghee; united are our heroes in me and the cattle in their herdsman.

sanskrit: ā harāmi gavāṃ kṣīram āhārṣaṃ dhānyaṃ rasam | āhārṣam asmākaṃ vīrān ā patnīm edam astakam ||
english: I bring hither the milk of the cattle; I have brought hither the essence of grain; I have brought hither our heroes, and the wife — this is the oblation.
